Samir — great conversation today, thanks for the context. Below is a concise recap from our call and proposed next steps so your team has something to take to InfoSec/procurement.

Recap (what we heard)
- Current stack:
  - OpenAI (chat completions / gpt-4.1) for clinical summarization pipelines (batch + nearline).
  - Anthropic for assistant/triage flows in pilot (conversational).
  - In-house ETL and prompt templates; significant pre/post-processing.
- Pain points:
  - Vendor lock and desire to run open models (compliance & cost control).
  - Cost: batch summarization spikes causing unpredictable spend.
  - Rate limits/concurrency issues impacting nightly batch windows.
  - Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence, data residency, and support for customer-managed keys.
- Success criteria for a migration POC:
  1) Accuracy parity on a held-out clinical summary eval set (target: score within 2% of current baseline).
  2) Token/unit cost reduction of ~3x on batch workloads.
  3) Interactive latency p50 <= 300ms for 1k token contexts.
  4) Equivalent or improved operational reliability and observability (tracing, per-route metrics).

Compatibility/constraints
- Model API surface needs: chat-style completions, streaming tokens, and embeddings endpoint for retrieval.
- Tokenizer compatibility: must support conversion from existing OpenAI prompts with minimal re-tuning.
- Quantization tolerance: ability to run FP16/8 quantized variants for cost reduction.

Shortlist (initial models to evaluate)
- Llama 2 (70B / 13B distilled) — good baseline for parity testing.
- Mistral Instruct / Mixtral variants — strong instruction-following at favorable compute cost.
- Falcon 40B / 7B — strong open-source performance on summarization.
- Red team / safety notes: include Anthropic-style safety wrapper; we recommend sandboxed evals before production.

Proposed PoC outline
- Phase 0 (1 week): access & security — provide SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration options, and narrow network/IP allowlist for test endpoints.
- Phase 1 (2–3 weeks): model parity PoC — run held-out evals on Llama 2 & Mistral variants, basic latency/cost profiling.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): integration & stress tests — batch throughput testing, concurrency tests, and streaming latency.
- Deliverables: evaluation report, recommended model/profile, config for batching/quantization, and a cost estimate for production run.

Attachments shared with this note: redwood-technical-overview.pdf (high-level architecture), redwood-soc2-evidence.zip (SOC2 summary & artifacts). I also uploaded a sample PoC checklist to the Drive — link below.

Next steps / asks
- Samir: confirm PoC timeline and whether Priya (procurement) should be looped in now for contract terms.
- Acme: share the held-out eval set (or a sample) and a rough monthly baseline token volume for batch jobs.
- Redwood (Aditya): follow up with a short technical plan and a model-inference cost estimate.

Samir — quick technical follow-up / additions to Marissa's recap:

- Tokenizer note: in our experience Llama/Mistral tokenization is close enough for most prompt templates; we usually run a small auto-tuning pass for stop sequences and system messages.
- Latency: For interactive paths we recommend a dedicated low-latency pool (pinned instances) for p50 <= 300ms at 1–2 rps/user. Batch jobs benefit more from larger reserved capacity with autoscaling.
- Quantization: 8-bit quantization yields ~3–4x cost improvements with small accuracy delta on summarization; we'll include model-specific quant profiles in the PoC.

I attached a short tech plan and cost sketch to the Drive folder — will share a PDF later today.

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
